summary: TritonShip production: heartbeat fanout storm caused duplicate completions, invoice exposure, and urgent customer escalation
description: Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 12:10 UTC TritonShip reported elevated duplicate completions and unexpected billing spikes. Root symptom: a rapid series of heartbeat retries from the multiplexer combined with stale multipath routing state causing fanout amplification and duplicated completions returned to the customer. Impact: Several thousand requests for a high-volume batch job returned duplicate tokens; TritonShip reported customers seeing duplicated invoices and increased token consumption estimates. Timeline (high-level): 2026-03-10 12:04 UTC - TritonShip job started; 12:07 UTC - increased heartbeat RTTs observed; 12:10 UTC - TritonShip opened support with sample transcript showing duplicated responses; 12:14 UTC - automated throttles began triggering; 12:18 UTC - on-call SRE engaged and temporarily disabled aggressive heartbeat retries; 12:40 UTC - safe mode routing rolled out; 13:05 UTC - fix deployed to multiplexer; 14:30 UTC - customer confirmed reduced duplicates; 15:00 UTC - incident declared resolved. Environment: prod, us-east region, dedicated enterprise capacity for TritonShip. Steps to reproduce (internal): 1) simulate rapid session reconnects with small jitter (100-300ms) from multiple frontends; 2) force stale route cache on multiplexer (race in route refresh); 3) trigger concurrent KV cache priming with prefix overlap; 4) observe duplicate completions and repro token accounting mismatch. Observed behavior: duplicate completions with identical message IDs returned to customer, billing meter counted both completions; streaming clients experienced interleaved progress frames leading to partial re-transmit. Immediate mitigation: 1) throttled heartbeat retries at ingress for TritonShip; 2) enabled idempotency dedupe at multiplexer for 30m window; 3) rolled safe-mode routing to single-path for affected customer capacity; 4) issued temporary billing credit for the window pending reconciliation. Customer communication: initial notice sent 2026-03-10 12:28 UTC acknowledging impact and mitigation steps; follow-up timeline and temporary credit offer sent 2026-03-10 15:20 UTC; post-incident report shared 2026-03-12 with RCA and permanent mitigations.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy heartbeats causing request duplication at ingress layer. Evidence did not fully support ingress-only; multiplexer logs showed repeated handoffs for same session id.

Found race in multiplexer route refresh: concurrent refresh + in-flight fanout triggered duplicate backend writes for the same logical request. Route refresh TTL reduction in prior week increased refresh frequency under load.
KV prefix priming was observed concurrently leading to duplicated tokens when multiple backends responded nearly simultaneously; dedupe threshold missing for inflight request dedup key.

Telemetry: aggregated rate of duplicate completion events peaked at 3.8% of TritonShip requests during 12:07-12:22 UTC window (baseline <0.01%). Billing meter double-counted completions due to duplicate acknowledgement flow in billing pipeline.
Related config change: route-cache-ttl reduced from 60s to 10s in last week's canary (INT-55890). That change increased the opportunity for race under transient heartbeat jitter.
resolution: Short-term: throttled heartbeat retries on TritonShip ingress, enabled 30m idempotency dedupe window, and routed TritonShip traffic to single-path until fix verified. Issued pro-rata credit covering duplicated token window.

Permanent fix: multiplexer patch (v3.15.0) implementing atomic route refresh, per-request dedupe key, and safe guard against concurrent backend fanout duplication. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1298

Rollout notes: staged canary to 5% on 2026-03-12 10:00 UTC, increased to 50% after 30m with no regression, full rollout by 2026-03-12 14:00 UTC. Billing reconciliation job completed 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC and credits applied.
Post-incident: TritonShip confirmed reduced duplication and accepted credit; incident closed but monitoring will remain elevated for two weeks.
follow_up_actions: INT-55890 review: revert or re-evaluate route-cache-ttl change and improve canary checks for route-refresh frequency.
Add synthetic test for heartbeat jitter + route-refresh race to CI (owner: QA).
Billing pipeline: add dedupe protection for near-duplicate completion events to avoid double-charging (owner: Billing).
Update runbook: guidance for safe-mode single-path routing and customer communication templates for duplication incidents (owner: SRE/CS).
Monitor dashboard: add duplicate-completion rate alert (threshold 0.1%) for dedicated pools.
